passages.text:
The following text is from an original short story.
Marisol had expected the abandoned greenhouse to be empty, but it was ______ with life: ferns crowded every bench, and vines had climbed all the way to the cracked glass roof.

passages.title: Foundations
passages.text: Bridges are usually admired for their spans, the distances between their supports. Engineer Tomás Reyes, however, argues that the most important part of a bridge is the part no one sees: its foundation. "A long span on a weak foundation," he says, "is simply a dramatic way to fail."
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Repair café
passages.text: Once a month, a community center in the town of Alder Creek hosts a "repair café," where volunteers fix residents' broken lamps, toasters, and bicycles for free. Organizers say the event keeps hundreds of items out of the landfill each year. Just as important, they add, residents who watch the repairs often learn to fix similar problems on their own.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Feeder survey
passages.text:
A student counted the birds visiting three feeders in her yard over four weeks. Each feeder held a different food.
Feeder | Food | Total visits
1 | Sunflower seeds | 212
2 | Thistle seeds | 87
3 | Suet | 145
The student concluded that, of the three foods, sunflower seeds attracted the most visits.

passages.text:

• Glass bottles and plastic bottles can both be recycled.

• Recycled glass is often used to make new bottles.

passages.title: Tardigrades
passages.text: For years, many biologists assumed that tardigrades, tiny animals that can survive being almost completely dried out, protected themselves mainly by producing a sugar called trehalose, which helps shield cells in some other organisms. Yet when researchers measured trehalose in several tardigrade species, they found little or none. Further work identified proteins found only in tardigrades that form a glass-like gel as the animals dry, apparently protecting their cells until water returns.

passages.title: Learning words (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
Some teachers argue that the fastest way for students to build vocabulary is to memorize lists of words and their definitions. Students can review dozens of words in a single sitting, and quiz scores often rise within days.

Text 2
Researchers who study reading point out that definitions memorized for a quiz are often forgotten within weeks. Words met repeatedly in meaningful reading, by contrast, tend to be retained, because readers see how the words are actually used.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Shell chains
passages.text: Marine biologists have observed that when an empty shell larger than any in a group appears, hermit crabs nearby often line up by size beside it. When the largest crab moves into the new shell, the next crab in line takes the shell it left behind, and so on down the line. This pattern suggests that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Historian
passages.text: Unlike earlier accounts of the mill town's decline, which blamed a single cause, the historian's new study is notably ______: she weighs several possible explanations and openly acknowledges the limits of the surviving records.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Highway lanes (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
Some transportation planners argue that adding lanes to a congested highway reduces traffic. As evidence, they point to a widening project after which average travel times on the highway fell during the following year.

Text 2
Researchers who study "induced demand" report that when lanes are added to congested highways, travel times often improve at first, but within a few years the new lanes tend to fill as more people choose to drive, and congestion returns to roughly its earlier level.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.text:

Town | Visits in 2019 | Visits in 2023
A | 12,000 | 15,000
B | 30,000 | 34,500
C | 8,000 | 10,400
The researcher noted that the town with the largest percentage increase in visits was not the town with the largest increase in the number of visits.

passages.text: Divers spent three seasons excavating a merchant ship that sank off the coast more than two thousand years ago. passages.title: Songbird migration notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A researcher tracked two populations of a migratory songbird.
• One population nests in Norway; the other nests in Spain.
• Both populations spend the winter in West Africa.
• The Norwegian birds left West Africa an average of 9 days earlier than the Spanish birds.
• The Norwegian birds reached their nesting grounds an average of 11 days later than the Spanish birds.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Marsh grazing
passages.text: In one salt marsh, ecologists fenced snails out of some plots of cordgrass and left other plots open. After a season, the fenced plots held dense cordgrass, while many open plots had been grazed bare. In a nearby marsh where snail-eating crabs are abundant, however, the open plots looked nearly identical to the fenced ones. These results suggest that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Songbird pitch
passages.text: Ecologist Dara Mensah studies a songbird whose city populations sing at a higher pitch than its rural populations. Many researchers attribute the difference to traffic noise, which masks low-pitched sounds. Mensah instead hypothesizes that young birds simply learn the songs of the adults around them, and that the first birds to settle in the city happened to sing at a higher pitch.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Late quartets
passages.text: Composer Lena Ostrova's early string quartets were praised for their dense counterpoint, with all four instruments carrying independent melodies at once. Her later quartets abandon that density, often giving a single melody to one instrument while the others hold long, quiet chords. Some critics have called this change a decline in ambition. Ostrova's sketchbooks, however, show that she revised these sparse passages more times than any of her earlier music.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Committee report
passages.text: Although the committee's final report ran to more than two hundred pages, its recommendations were notably ______: each could be carried out within a single budget year by the city's existing staff.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Crater streaks
passages.text: For years, dark streaks that appear on the walls of certain Martian craters were widely thought to be traces of flowing salty water. When planetary scientist Teodor Lind compared the streaks' locations with maps of slope, however, he found that they occur only on slopes steep enough for dry sand and dust to slide on their own. Lind argues that the streaks are better explained as small avalanches of dry material.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Four-day week (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
Economist Rosa Iglesias argues that a four-day workweek raises productivity. She points to a group of firms where output per hour rose after employees switched to working four days a week.

Text 2
Labor researchers note that the firms volunteering for four-day-week trials tend to be ones whose managers already expect the change to succeed and whose work can easily be compressed into fewer days. Results from such firms, the researchers caution, may not hold for workplaces in general.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.text:
A researcher measured the percentage of seeds that germinated for two wildflower species at three soil temperatures.
Soil temperature | Species X | Species Y
10°C | 12% | 40%
18°C | 55% | 62%
26°C | 81% | 58%
The researcher claims that Species X's germination is more sensitive to soil temperature than Species Y's is.

Herders who raise animals mainly for meat tend to slaughter them young, whatever their sex, whereas herders who keep animals for milk tend to keep females into adulthood and cull most young males. The pattern in the village therefore suggests that ______

passages.title: Covered market
passages.text: Many visitors to the old covered market in Varos assume that its maze of alleys grew without any plan. Historian Selin Aydın's study of property records complicates that view. The market's oldest section, she found, was laid out on a deliberate grid around two stone storehouses; only the later additions, built as trade expanded, wandered outward along whatever streets already existed.

passages.title: Cholera map
passages.text: In the 1850s, many physicians in London held that cholera spread through foul air. During an 1854 outbreak, physician John Snow mapped the homes of those who died and found that they clustered around a single public water pump. Workers at a nearby brewery, who drank the beer they were given rather than water from the pump, were largely spared. Snow's findings pointed to contaminated water, not air, as the source.

passages.title: The letter
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story. Mrs. Hale has just received a letter.
She read the letter twice, the second time more slowly, as though the words might rearrange themselves into something kinder if given the opportunity. They did not. She folded it along its creases, laid it upon the mantel beside the clock, and turned to the window, where the afternoon was going about its business with a composure she could not help resenting.

But because the second group consists entirely of people who chose not to buy, the difference may instead reflect the fact that ______

• It had remained unsolved for 70 years.
• Okonjo's proof uses a technique from probability theory.

passages.title: Printing press
passages.text: Many historians have argued that the printing press spread quickly across Europe because it dramatically lowered the cost of books. Historian Imre Halasz agrees that printing eventually made books cheaper, but he notes that in the first decades after its introduction, printed books often sold for about as much as manuscripts did. He also observes that the earliest presses clustered in cities that already had universities and established book trades.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Cat domestication
passages.text: Early accounts portrayed the domestication of cats as deliberate: people, it was said, tamed wild cats to protect stored grain from rodents. Genetic studies have complicated this picture. Domestic cats show far fewer genetic differences from their wild ancestors than domestic dogs do from theirs, and those differences arose gradually over thousands of years. Some researchers now argue that cats largely domesticated themselves, tolerating people in exchange for easy access to prey, long before humans took any deliberate role in their breeding.

• Composer Daniel Oyelaran wrote the opera Harbor Lights (2004).
• Salt Road is set in a nineteenth-century mining town; Harbor Lights is set in a modern port city.

passages.title: Night heat
passages.text: Most studies of urban heat have focused on daytime temperatures. Yet for human health, nighttime temperatures may matter more, because the body recovers from daytime heat stress only when temperatures fall after dark. Climatologist Kofi Asante's measurements show that in dense neighborhoods, pavement and buildings release stored heat at night, keeping nights as much as 5°C warmer than in nearby parks.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Salmon decline
passages.text: For decades, the decline of salmon in the Varna River was blamed on overfishing. When fishing limits were tightened in the 1990s, however, salmon numbers kept falling. Biologist Mara Lindqvist then noticed that the decline closely tracked the construction of small dams on the river's tributaries, which block salmon from reaching their spawning streams. Since several of those dams were removed in 2015, salmon counts in the affected tributaries have tripled.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.text:
The following text is from a short story. Inés has recently moved from her grandmother's rural home to a city apartment.
At night the building was never quiet. Pipes knocked in the walls, a neighbor's television murmured through the floor, and the elevator groaned between stories. Inés had expected to find the noise unbearable. Instead, lying awake on the third night, she realized she had been listening for it, the way she had once listened for the creek behind her grandmother's house.

passages.title: Irrigation yields
passages.text:

Crop | Without irrigation | With irrigation

Barley | 25 | 41
Oats | 28 | 36
The researcher claimed that the crop with the greatest increase from irrigation was also the crop with the lowest yield without irrigation.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Two valleys
passages.text: Linguists studying a language spoken in two neighboring valleys found that speakers in the eastern valley use a word for "river" borrowed from a neighboring language, while speakers in the western valley use an older native word. Historical records show that the eastern valley was a regional trading center for centuries, while the western valley was relatively isolated. These findings suggest that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Mayor visit
passages.text: The mayor, along with three members of the city council and two engineers from the state transportation department, ______ scheduled to tour the flooded neighborhood on Monday morning.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Tool kit
passages.text: The basic repair kit sold at the hardware store includes several ______ a wrench, a level, a utility knife, and a twenty-five-foot tape measure.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Early telescopes
passages.text: Early telescopes produced blurry images because different colors of light passing through a lens came into focus at slightly different points. ______ astronomers often had to choose between a bright image and a sharp one, since reducing the blur also meant letting in less light.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bike lanes (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
A downtown business owner argues that replacing street parking with bike lanes will hurt local shops, because most customers arrive by car and will go elsewhere if they cannot park.

Text 2
Studies of similar changes in several cities found that shop revenue on affected streets usually rose. Cyclists tended to spend somewhat less per visit than drivers, but they visited more often.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Learning grammar (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
A linguist argues that young children learn the grammar of their first language mainly because adults correct their grammatical mistakes.

Text 2
Researchers who recorded hundreds of hours of conversation between parents and young children found that parents rarely corrected grammatical errors; they usually corrected statements that were factually wrong instead. The children nevertheless acquired their language's grammar on a typical schedule.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Lost blueprints
passages.text: Because the bridge's original blueprints had been lost decades earlier, engineers could only ______ how its internal supports were arranged, inferring the layout from patterns of cracks visible on the surface.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Childhood kitchen
passages.text:
The following text is from a novel. Teodor is visiting the house where he grew up.
The kitchen was smaller than he remembered. In his mind the table had stood like an island in a wide room, with space enough for his brothers to chase one another around it. Now he could nearly touch both walls by stretching out his arms, and the table, pushed against the window, could seat only three.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Distant stone
passages.text: Archaeologists long assumed that the stone tools found at a hilltop site had been made there. Chemical analysis, however, shows that the stone came from a quarry about 300 kilometers away. Moreover, the site contains almost no waste flakes, the small chips that are produced in large numbers whenever stone tools are shaped. These findings suggest that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Reef scientist
passages.text: The marine biologist ______ the grant committee selected to lead the new reef survey has studied coral bleaching in the western Pacific for nearly two decades.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Carson book
passages.text: Rachel Carson wrote several books about the natural world. Her ______ published in 1962, drew public attention to the dangers of pesticides and helped launch the modern environmental movement.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Nurse sharks
passages.text: Many species of shark must keep swimming to push water over their gills and take in oxygen. ______ nurse sharks can rest motionless on the seafloor for long periods, using muscles in their mouths to pump water over their gills.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Printing press
passages.text: Many histories describe the printing press as a sudden break with the past. Historian Ada Lindqvist disagrees. She points out that for decades before the press, workshops had been producing books by printing from carved wooden blocks, and that early printers deliberately designed their pages to resemble handwritten manuscripts. The press, in her account, sped up changes that were already under way rather than starting them.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Glacier notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Glaciers in the Arven Range have lost about 40% of their area since 1950.
• Average summer temperatures there have risen by 1.5°C over the same period.
• Researchers attribute most of the glacier loss to longer melt seasons.
• Melt seasons in the range now begin about three weeks earlier than in 1950.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Unmoved characters
passages.text: Critics found the director's latest film strangely ______: although its plot is crowded with explosions and chases, its characters display almost no emotion, greeting each new disaster with the same mild interest.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Reproduced results
passages.text: The chemist's early claims about the new catalyst were initially met with skepticism, but they were ______ by later experiments, which reproduced her results in three independent laboratories.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Hidden letters
passages.text: Beneath the floorboards of the old farmhouse ______ a bundle of letters and two photographs that had been hidden there for nearly a century.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Two researchers
passages.text: The two ______ findings, published a month apart, seemed to contradict each other until a third team showed that the studies had measured soil moisture at different depths.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Trees and asthma
passages.text: A city found that children in neighborhoods with many street trees had lower rates of asthma than children in neighborhoods with few trees. A council member concluded that planting more trees would reduce childhood asthma. The tree-lined neighborhoods, however, also had ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Light and growth
passages.text:
A botanist grew three plant species under red, blue, and white light and recorded average height, in centimeters, after six weeks.
Species | Red | Blue | White
X | 20 | 18 | 15
Y | 14 | 17 | 12
Z | 25 | 21 | 19
A student claims that red light produced the tallest plants for every species in the study.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Seventy-year dictionary
passages.text: The first edition of one major English dictionary took about seventy years to complete, from the collection of the first quotations to the publication of the final volume. ______ by the time the last volume appeared, the earliest volumes were already out of date, missing words that had entered the language in the meantime.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Museum notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Harlan Museum displays each object with only a short label giving its name and date.
• Curators there want visitors to form their own impressions before reading about an object.
• The Ostrova Museum places a long text panel and an audio guide beside each object.
• Curators there want visitors to understand each object's history in detail.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Solar storm
passages.text: In 1859, a powerful solar storm produced auroras visible as far south as the Caribbean. Telegraph operators reported sparks leaping from their equipment, and some found they could send messages even after disconnecting their batteries. Scientists today estimate that a storm of similar strength would seriously damage modern power grids and satellites.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Crow study notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers wore a distinctive mask while trapping and banding several wild crows.
• The crows were then released unharmed.
• In later years, crows on the campus scolded and dived at people wearing that mask.
• The crows largely ignored people wearing a different mask.
• Researchers concluded that crows can recognize and remember individual human faces.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Guarded statements
passages.text: Though the senator's public statements on the trade agreement were carefully ______, leaving reporters unsure whether she supported it, her private letters, released decades later, reveal that she had opposed it from the start.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Four-day week
passages.text:
Text 1
Several economists argue that a four-day workweek can raise productivity. They point to trials in which companies cut weekly hours by a fifth while total output stayed about the same, meaning that each hour of work produced more than before.
Text 2
A labor researcher who reviewed the same trials notes that nearly all of the participating companies were office-based firms that chose to volunteer. Firms confident that their work could be compressed, she observes, were the ones most likely to sign up.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The baker's step
passages.text: In a short story, the narrator describes her neighbor Mrs. Okafor as someone who concealed her generosity behind a stern manner.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Two portraits
passages.text: Of the two portraits the museum acquired last year, the one ______ in the east wing was long attributed to a little-known painter; recent analysis of its pigments suggests that it was painted by the workshop's founder herself.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bridge cables
passages.text: The engineers tested the bridge's cables for corrosion ______ replaced the three that showed the most wear before reopening the bridge to traffic.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A rushed ending
passages.text: Critics argue that the novel's ending is rushed, resolving in two pages a conflict that took three hundred to build. ______ the ending's abruptness may be deliberate: the author has said she wanted readers to feel as unprepared for the resolution as the characters are.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Return to the village
passages.text:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Teodora has returned to her childhood village after twenty years away.
She had expected the village to be smaller, the way places from childhood are said to shrink. Instead it seemed larger, emptier. The bakery where she had bought bread every morning was shuttered, and the square where children once played was now a parking lot. She walked its length twice, as though the old square might be hiding beneath the painted lines, and then stood for a long time by the fountain, the only thing she recognized, listening to its water fall the way it always had.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Commuting modes
passages.text:
A transportation researcher compared how commuters in one city traveled to work in 2015 and 2023.
Mode | 2015 (%) | 2023 (%)
Car | 62 | 54
Bus | 18 | 15
Bicycle | 6 | 14
Walking | 14 | 17
The researcher claims that, over this period, the share of commuters who cycled grew by more percentage points than the share for any other way of commuting.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Ancient oats
passages.text: Archaeologists have found grinding stones bearing traces of wild oat starch at a site occupied about 32,000 years ago, long before oats were domesticated. Because the starch grains show signs of having been heated before they were ground, the researchers suggest that the site's inhabitants ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Learning words
passages.text: Some linguists argue that young children learn new words mainly by hearing them repeated; others argue that children learn words mainly by inferring their meanings from context. A study of toddlers complicates both views: it found that repetition mattered more for learning nouns, while context mattered more for learning verbs.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A careful historian
passages.text: Reviewers noted that the historian's account of the expedition's failure is deliberately ______: she meticulously lays out the evidence for each competing explanation but never indicates which one she finds most convincing.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Late poems
passages.text: Although the poet's early work was widely imitated, her later poems were so ______ that few readers, let alone imitators, could follow their dense allusions to obscure medieval texts.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Caffeinated nectar
passages.text: Some flowering plants produce small amounts of caffeine in their nectar, which might seem likely to deter pollinators, since caffeine tastes bitter. In experiments, however, bees that fed on nectar containing low doses of caffeine were more likely to remember and return to the scent of that flower than bees fed on nectar without caffeine. This suggests that, for the plants, caffeine in nectar may ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The treaty debate
passages.text: Historians have long argued ______ the treaty's harsh terms, rather than any single political leader, made the war that followed nearly inevitable.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Sensitive periods
passages.text: In the 1950s, researchers found that some songbirds learn their songs by imitating adult birds during a sensitive period early in life; birds that hear no adult song then never sing normally. ______ human infants appear to learn the sounds of their native language most easily within their first year.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Hummingbird notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Most hummingbirds weigh less than 6 grams.
• Scientists once doubted that birds so small could store enough fat to fly long distances.
• Rufous hummingbirds migrate up to about 6,000 kilometers between Alaska and Mexico.
• Researchers track hummingbirds by attaching tiny numbered bands to their legs.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The cello
passages.text:
The following text is adapted from a short story.
For weeks Ana's scales sounded like a door creaking in the wind. She practiced them anyway, every evening, while her brother complained through the wall. Then one night in March she played the C major scale and stopped halfway, startled. The note had not creaked. It had simply rung, clear and round, and for a moment she was afraid to play the next one in case it would not.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bike lanes and injuries
passages.text:
Text 1
Many urban planners credit networks of protected bike lanes with reducing traffic injuries. They point to several cities where reported injuries fell sharply in the years after extensive lane networks were built.
Text 2
A transportation economist observes that the cities that built extensive bike lanes also lowered their speed limits during those same years. Lower speed limits on their own, she notes, have been linked to large drops in traffic injuries.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Regrowing limbs
passages.text: Early naturalists regarded the axolotl's ability to regrow lost limbs as an ______, a strange exception among animals with backbones, but biologists now know that several other salamanders share the ability.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Seedling density
passages.text:
Researchers planted tree seedlings at four densities and recorded the percentage still alive after one year.
Seedlings planted per square meter | 10 | 20 | 40 | 80
Percentage surviving | 90% | 75% | 55% | 40%
A student claims that even though the survival rate fell as density increased, the number of surviving seedlings per square meter rose.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bright plumage
passages.text: In many bird species, males with brighter plumage attract more mates, but bright colors also make males easier for predators to spot. If predation is what keeps male plumage from becoming even brighter, then researchers studying a population of one such species on an island with no bird predators would expect males there to ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Restoring the mills
passages.text: Restoring the town's three abandoned textile mills, along with the network of canals that once powered their looms, ______ more than a decade and cost nearly twice the original estimate.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The Rosetta Stone
passages.text: The Rosetta Stone ______ in 1799 by French soldiers near the Egyptian town of Rashid, carries the same decree in three scripts, a feature that later helped scholars decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bamboo
passages.text: Bamboo grows remarkably quickly, with some species reaching their full height in a single growing season. ______ it can be harvested without killing the plant, which sends up new shoots from its underground roots.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Muralist notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Elena Varga (1921–1987) was a Hungarian-born muralist who worked in Chicago.
• Her best-known work, Harvest Line, covers a 200-foot wall of a former rail depot.
• The mural shows grain workers loading freight cars.
• Varga painted it in 1958 using donated house paint.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Rising bedrock
passages.text: For decades, geologists assumed that the bedrock beneath large ice sheets rose only very slowly after the ice above it thinned. Recent measurements beneath part of the West Antarctic Ice Sheet, however, show the ground there rising by several centimeters a year as the ice thins, because the underlying rock flows unusually easily. Some researchers suggest that this rapid rise could eventually help slow the ice sheet's retreat by lifting the base of the ice.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Teaching methods
passages.text:
A district compared average test scores of students taught with two reading methods at urban and rural schools.
School type | Method A | Method B
Urban | 72 | 75
Rural | 64 | 73
A researcher claims that Method B's advantage over Method A was greater at rural schools than at urban schools.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Kangaroo rats
passages.text: Desert kangaroo rats rarely drink water. Instead, they obtain it from the seeds they eat, partly from the moisture in the seeds and partly from water their bodies produce as they break down food. Their long nasal passages also cool each exhaled breath, so that much of its moisture condenses and is reabsorbed before it can escape.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A dim star
passages.text: Astronomers long assumed that a certain dim star appeared faint simply because it was small. A later explanation proposed instead that a thick cloud of dust surrounds the star and blocks much of its light. Measurements of the star's infrared glow, which is produced when dust absorbs starlight and re-emits it as heat, have since supported the dust explanation.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Rainfall records
passages.text: Having studied the region's rainfall records for more than three decades, ______ that droughts there now last, on average, about twice as long as they did in the 1970s.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: An inaccurate globe
passages.text: The museum's newest acquisition—a nineteenth-century globe showing several coastlines that later surveys proved inaccurate______ is displayed near the main entrance.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Naming a species
passages.text: The two researchers who first described the tiny freshwater snail in 2019 ______ it after the river where they found it, a stretch of water that had not been surveyed in decades.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Waiting hikers
passages.text: By the time the rescue team reached the ridge, the two hikers ______ beneath a rock ledge for nearly two days, rationing the little food they had left.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Color words
passages.text:
Text 1
In a famous study, two researchers proposed that languages add basic color words in a predictable order: a word for red appears before a word for green or yellow, and a word for blue comes later still. They based this order on a comparison of nearly one hundred languages.
Text 2
Later linguists noted that most of the languages in that comparison were widely spoken and often written, and that the researchers relied in many cases on a single speaker per language. When these linguists studied languages with fewer speakers in greater depth, several did not follow the proposed order.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The speech
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story.
Mara had practiced the speech for three weeks, until she could recite it without looking. When she reached the podium, she set her notes face down, looked out at the rows of folding chairs, and began, instead, to talk about her grandmother.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Seven volumes
passages.text: Reviewers called the biographer's account ______: across seven volumes it records nearly every letter the composer wrote, every rehearsal she attended, and every illness she suffered.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The negotiator
passages.text: Observers described the negotiator's manner as ______: although she firmly rejected each of the union's demands, she did so with such courtesy and tact that the meeting ended in handshakes.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A quiet mayor
passages.text: Unlike his ______ predecessor, who held a press conference to announce even the most minor decisions and seemed never to tire of speaking to reporters, the new mayor rarely gave interviews.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Library hours
passages.text:
After a public library began staying open until 9:00 p.m. on weekdays, a researcher compared its average monthly visits before and after the change.
Time period | Before | After
Weekday mornings | 120 | 118
Weekday evenings | 60 | 145
Weekends | 200 | 210
The researcher claims that the extended evening hours, rather than a general rise in interest in the library, account for most of the increase in visits.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Fig wasps
passages.text: Some species of fig tree are pollinated by only a single species of tiny wasp, and that wasp can reproduce only inside the figs of that tree species. Because of this close dependence, a sharp decline in the wasp population would most likely ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A growing main street
passages.text: The town's population fell by about a third between 1990 and 2010. ______ the number of businesses on its main street nearly doubled over the same period, as tourists began visiting its restored historic district.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Ancient gears
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Antikythera mechanism is an ancient Greek device recovered from a shipwreck in 1901.
• It contains at least 30 interlocking bronze gears.
• Turning a hand crank moved the gears, which advanced pointers on dials.
• The pointers showed the positions of the Sun and Moon in the sky.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A museum collection
passages.text: Since 2015, the city's history museum ______ more than forty paintings by local artists, many of them donated by the artists' families.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Twelve paintings
passages.text: The gallery's most popular room displays a cycle of twelve paintings by a seventeenth-century Flemish artist. Each of the twelve paintings ______ a different month of the year through the work done in the fields at that time.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Solar siblings
passages.text: Most stars form in clusters from the same cloud of gas, but over hundreds of millions of years the members of a cluster drift apart. Astronomers comparing the chemical makeup of nearby stars with that of the Sun have identified a few whose compositions are nearly identical to the Sun's, which suggests that they formed in the same cloud. Studying these "solar siblings" could help researchers reconstruct the environment in which the Sun was born.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Sheep and faces
passages.text: An animal behaviorist hypothesizes that sheep identify familiar people mainly by their faces rather than by other cues, such as voice, clothing, or smell.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bridge reviews
passages.text: Early reviews of the bridge's design were ______: engineers praised its daring, record-setting span while warning that its slender supports might not survive a strong earthquake.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Screen time and sleep
passages.text:
A researcher surveyed students about their daily screen time, their average nightly sleep, and their scores on a reading test.
Daily screen time | Average sleep (hours) | Average test score
Less than 1 hour | 8.2 | 84
1 to 3 hours | 7.6 | 81
More than 3 hours | 6.9 | 76
The researcher notes that students who reported more screen time also reported less sleep.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Inland clay
passages.text: Archaeologists studying a coastal settlement found that its pottery was made from a type of clay that occurs only in deposits about 300 kilometers inland. The settlement's residents left no tools, paths, or other evidence of travel to the interior, so the researchers concluded that the residents most likely ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Desert plants
passages.text: Many desert plants store water in thick, fleshy stems or leaves. ______ they can survive long periods with no rainfall at all.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A late start
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Ynes Mexia (1870–1938) was a Mexican American botanist.
• She began collecting plants professionally in her mid-fifties.
• Over the next thirteen years, she gathered about 145,000 plant specimens.
• About 500 of the species she collected were new to science.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Urban birdsong
passages.text: A number of recent studies ______ that birds living in noisy cities tend to sing at higher pitches than birds of the same species living in quieter rural areas.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bridge inspectors
passages.text: The team of engineers that inspects the city's oldest bridge ______ a detailed report to the city council every spring, listing any repairs that should be made before winter.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Remote glaciers
passages.text: Satellite measurements show that many mountain glaciers have been shrinking for decades. For example, glaciers in the Alps have lost roughly half of their volume since the mid-1800s. Not all glaciers are retreating at the same rate, however; a few in high, snowy ranges have remained nearly stable.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The fast year
passages.text: In a poem, the speaker expresses surprise at how quickly the seasons pass.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Ordered clashes
passages.text: Although the composer's early critics dismissed her harmonies as merely ______, later scholars showed that every apparent clash in her music followed strict rules she had worked out in her notebooks.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Dating with lichens
passages.text: When a rockslide exposes fresh stone, lichens soon begin to colonize the bare surfaces. Some lichens grow at a slow and fairly steady rate, often only a fraction of a millimeter per year. By measuring the largest lichens on boulders from an undated rockslide and comparing them with lichens on surfaces of known age, such as dated gravestones, geologists can estimate roughly when the slide occurred.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Beetles under snow
passages.text: The larvae of a certain beetle spend the winter in the soil and die if the soil temperature falls below about −5°C. In one mountain valley, researchers found that larval survival dropped sharply during a winter with unusually little snow, even though average air temperatures that winter were milder than usual. This finding suggests that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Water tower
passages.text: The engineer who designed the town's first water tower ______ the structure would last a century; it was finally replaced in 2019, 104 years after it was built.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The Ferrer sisters
passages.text: Born a year apart, the painters Ana and Lucía Ferrer worked side by side for four decades. The ______ shared studio, a converted bakery in Valencia, is now a small museum.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Telegraph ears
passages.text: Early telegraph operators were trained to transcribe incoming messages one letter at a time. Experienced operators, ______ often recognized whole words by the rhythm of their clicks and wrote them down before the final letters had even arrived.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Fog nets
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Fog harvesting is a technique for collecting water from fog.
• Fine-mesh nets are stretched across the path of fog blowing in from the sea.
• Water droplets collect on the mesh and drip into troughs below.
• Villages in parts of Chile's Atacama Desert have used fog harvesting to obtain drinking water.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: An open answer
passages.text: The ambassador's reply to the proposal was deliberately ______: it could be read either as acceptance or as refusal, which left both governments room to keep negotiating.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Counting steps
passages.text: Researchers hypothesized that desert ants find their way back to the nest partly by keeping track of the number of steps they have taken. To test this, they lengthened the legs of some ants with tiny stilts and shortened the legs of others after the ants had walked from the nest to a food source.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Sailors' letters
passages.text: The archive, which holds thousands of letters written by sailors to their families over two centuries, ______ open to researchers by appointment on weekdays.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Coating results
passages.text: The engineers tested a new coating on steel panels left outdoors near the ocean for a year. The results were ______ panels with the coating showed about half as much rust as uncoated panels.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Day-flying bats
passages.text: Most bats hunt at night, which lets them avoid hawks and other daytime predators. ______ a few species, such as some fruit bats on islands with no large predatory birds, regularly fly and feed during the day.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Late debut
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Penelope Fitzgerald published her first novel in 1977, at age 60.
• She won the Booker Prize two years later for Offshore.
• Laura Ingalls Wilder published her first novel, Little House in the Big Woods, in 1932, at age 65.
• Wilder's Little House books became classics of children's literature.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A town's decline (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
A historian argues that the plague of 1349 caused the decline of the market town of Hollin, which lost much of its population and trade in the years that followed.

Text 2
Tax records from Hollin show that the number of households paying the market tax fell steadily from about 1310 onward, as trade shifted to a new port downriver. The plague then sharply reduced a population that was already shrinking.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Ferry fares
passages.text:
After a ferry company cut its fares, it compared average daily ridership before and after the cut.
Season | Riders before cut | Riders after cut
Summer | 4,000 | 4,400
Winter | 1,000 | 1,300
A company analyst claims that, in percentage terms, the fare cut increased ridership more in winter than in summer.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Field notebooks
passages.text: The botanist's field notebooks were ______: every measurement was dated, labeled, and cross-referenced to the photograph of the plant it described.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The second sentence
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story.
Mara had rehearsed the speech all week. When the principal finally called her name, she walked to the microphone and found that the first sentence had vanished from her memory. She looked out at the rows of folding chairs. Then she began with the second sentence, and no one ever knew.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Library loans
passages.text:
A town library recorded the number of print and e-book loans each year.
Year | Print loans | E-book loans
2019 | 900 | 100
2020 | 600 | 400
2021 | 700 | 450
2022 | 750 | 500
A librarian claims that after a sharp drop in 2020, print loans partly recovered in the following years.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bare canvas (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
A critic argues that the bare patches of canvas in the painter's late works show that she was too ill to finish them, and that the paintings should be displayed with a note calling them incomplete.

Text 2
Conservators examining the late paintings with infrared imaging found detailed underdrawings that outline the bare patches precisely, along with the painter's written notes marking those areas "leave open."
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Reading room
passages.text: After a year of construction, the library opened a new ______ section with low shelves, beanbag chairs, and a small stage for story hours.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Stone mill
passages.text: Built in 1854 to grind wheat for the valley's farms, the stone mill on Fuller Creek ______ a pottery studio and a small gallery.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Island power
passages.text: Most of the island's electricity comes from wind turbines and solar panels; only about a tenth is generated by burning fuel. ______ roughly nine-tenths of the island's power is renewable.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Water hole cameras
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Researchers placed motion-sensing cameras at 40 water holes in a national park.
• The cameras recorded animal visits for 12 months.
• Elephants visited the water holes at night more often during the dry season.
• The researchers suggest that night visits help elephants avoid the heat.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Gym survey
passages.text: A survey of the members of a large gym found that 80 percent of them exercise at least four times a week. A city official cited this result as evidence that most of the city's residents exercise frequently. However, ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A revised date
passages.text: For decades, archaeologists dated a hilltop fort to about 500 BCE, relying on the style of pottery found inside its walls. Recently, a team used radiocarbon dating on charcoal from the fort's earliest hearths and obtained dates near 800 BCE. The team argues that the pottery style must have remained in use for far longer than previously assumed.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A hurried ending
passages.text: Many reviewers found the novel's ending ______: after three hundred pages of mounting tension, the central conflict was resolved in a single, hurried paragraph.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Trial policy
passages.text: The city's new parking policy was intended to be ______: it would remain in effect for only six months while officials studied its effects on traffic and local businesses.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Tasting arms
passages.text: Each sucker on an octopus's arms contains thousands of chemical receptors, allowing the animal to taste what it touches. Because a large share of an octopus's neurons are located in its arms rather than in its central brain, an arm can respond to a promising taste, for example by grasping, before the brain has fully processed the signal.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Shaded sidewalks
passages.text: A city planted trees along the north side of a long street but not along the south side. In summer, afternoon surface temperatures on the shaded north side were about 6°C lower than on the south side. Pedestrian counts showed about 40 percent more walkers on the north side in the afternoon, but no difference between the two sides in the early morning. These findings suggest that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Panel tilt
passages.text:
An engineer measured the yearly energy output of identical solar panels mounted at different tilt angles.
Tilt angle | Yearly output (kWh)
0° | 410
20° | 480
40° | 455
60° | 380
The engineer concludes that output was highest at an intermediate tilt rather than at either the smallest or the largest angle tested.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Ruins study
passages.text: Having studied the ruins for more than a decade, ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Canyon towers
passages.text: Along the canyon's northern rim ______ two stone towers that were built nearly a thousand years ago and are still largely intact.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Recycled asphalt
passages.text: Recycled asphalt usually costs less than newly produced asphalt. ______ it requires less energy to make, because much of the material has already been processed.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Raised dots
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Louis Braille was born in France in 1809.
• He lost his sight in an accident as a young child.
• At about age 15, he developed a writing system of raised dots.
• The system allowed blind people to read and write by touch.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Replica display
passages.text: Light gradually fades the colors of old textiles. For this reason, a museum that owns a fragile seventeenth-century tapestry displays a carefully made replica in its galleries, keeping the original in a dark storage room where researchers may view it by appointment.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Spare prose
passages.text: The essayist's prose is notably ______: she rarely uses a word that the sentence could do without, and many of her paragraphs consist of a single short sentence.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Warning colors
passages.text: Many poisonous animals display ______ coloring, such as bright orange or yellow bands, which makes them easy for predators to notice and, after one unpleasant encounter, to avoid.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Reef survey
passages.text: Most of the coral colonies in the survey area had recovered within five years of the bleaching event. The colonies on the reef's outer edge, ______ showed almost no recovery, possibly because warmer currents reached them first.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Probe journey
passages.text: A space probe launched in 2023 is expected to reach Jupiter in 2031. By the time it arrives, the probe ______ more than three billion kilometers, using the gravity of Earth and Venus to gain speed along the way.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Ceramic choice
passages.text: For the heat shield, the engineers tested more than forty materials, including several metals, carbon composites, and ceramics, under conditions that simulated reentry into the atmosphere. ______ they chose a ceramic tile that was slightly heavier than the best composite but far less likely to crack.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Fossil site notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2019, a team of paleontologists excavated a site in Montana.
• They found the nearly complete skeleton of a small horned dinosaur.
• The skeleton was preserved in fine river sediment.
• Nearly complete skeletons of horned dinosaurs are rare.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Mist and lichen
passages.text: In a forest, researchers found that a certain lichen grows mostly on the north sides of tree trunks, where the bark stays damp longest. Near a large waterfall in the same forest, however, where spray keeps every surface wet, the lichen grows on all sides of the trunks. These observations suggest that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The early route
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story.
For thirty-one years, Mr. Okafor had driven the number 9 bus, and for thirty-one years his alarm had rung at 4:30. He had been retired for a month now. Every morning he still woke at 4:29, a minute before the alarm he no longer set, and walked to the corner in time to watch the number 9 pull away without him.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The cast list
passages.text: Among the actors who auditioned for the role, the director chose Lena Ortiz, ______ performance in a small regional production had impressed critics the year before.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Diary entries
passages.text: The sea captain's diary is maddeningly ______: a storm that nearly sank the ship receives a single line, and a mutiny is recorded only as "trouble with the crew."
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Stone and steel
passages.text: The architect's library ______ local tradition: it is built from the region's gray fieldstone and topped with the steep roofs of nearby farmhouses, though its glass walls and sharp angles are unmistakably modern.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Trained bees
passages.text: Researchers trained bumblebees to find sugar water at blue disks. When the disks were then filled with plain water, the bees kept visiting them at first, but their visits dropped sharply after a few unrewarded trips. When sugar water was returned to the blue disks, visits rose again within a day. These results suggest that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Turbine output
passages.text:
An engineer recorded a wind turbine's power output at different wind speeds.
Wind speed (m/s) | Output (kW)
4 | 50
8 | 400
12 | 1,450
16 | 1,500
20 | 1,500
The engineer claims that output rose steeply between 8 and 12 meters per second but leveled off at higher wind speeds.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Island trails
passages.text: During the cleanup weekend, volunteers spent their time clearing fallen branches from the island's trails, repairing two footbridges, and ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Desert beetle
passages.text: The darkling beetle does not merely tolerate the heat of the Namib Desert. ______ it is most active at midday, when the sand's surface can exceed 60°C, foraging while many of its predators are sheltering from the sun.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Two great lakes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Lake Baikal, in Russia, is the deepest lake in the world.
• Its greatest depth is about 1,640 meters.
• Lake Superior, on the border of the United States and Canada, has the largest surface area of any freshwater lake.
• Lake Superior's greatest depth is about 400 meters.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The new coat
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story.
For three winters Nadia had worn her brother's old coat, its sleeves rolled twice at the cuffs. When her aunt finally sent money for a new one, Nadia took the bus downtown, tried on six coats, and came home with a thick blue one that fit. That night she hung it on the hook by the door, then took it down, put it on, and stood for a long time in front of the mirror in the hall.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Glacier lake
passages.text: As the glacier retreated over the last century, meltwater collected in the hollow it left behind and formed a lake that is now more than two kilometers ______ the lake did not exist on maps made before 1930.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Formats and genres
passages.text:
A library surveyed members about how many days they took, on average, to finish a book in print or as an audiobook.
Genre | Print (days) | Audiobook (days)
Novels | 9 | 6
Biography | 12 | 8
Poetry | 5 | 4.5
A librarian claims that audiobook listeners finished books faster than print readers in every genre, but that the difference was smallest for poetry.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Borrowed rhythms
passages.text: Critics agree that the young poet's first collection is largely ______: its rhythms, its images, and even several of its phrases are borrowed from the poets she most admired.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Early charts
passages.text: Many of the earliest charts of the region were ______: they placed some islands dozens of miles from their true positions and left others off entirely, errors that later surveys corrected one by one.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A disputed sitter (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
An art historian argues that a 1792 portrait of an unnamed young woman depicts the painter's sister, pointing to the strong resemblance between the sitter and the sister's known features.

Text 2
Letters in a family archive show that the painter's sister spent all of 1791 and 1792 abroad. The same letters mention that a neighbor sat for the painter several times during the winter of 1792.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Hidden nuts
passages.text: Gray squirrels bury thousands of nuts each autumn and recover many of them months later. To test how they find their caches, researchers moved the large stones and logs near some caches after the squirrels had buried nuts there. The squirrels still found those caches about as often as caches whose surroundings were left undisturbed. This result suggests that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bite force
passages.text: Although a spotted hyena is smaller than a lion, the bite force of a hyena is greater than ______ lion of comparable age, allowing it to crack bones that lions usually leave behind.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Coating tests
passages.text: In the laboratory, one group of engineers sprayed salt water on coated steel panels every hour for six weeks. ______ a second group placed identical panels on a pier by the ocean and checked them once a week for rust.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Fresco notes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• A fifteenth-century fresco covers the walls of a small chapel in central Italy.
• Conservators began restoring it in 2009.
• They removed centuries of grime by hand, a few square centimeters at a time.
• The restoration was completed in 2021.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Bacteria experiment
passages.text: Because the samples had been contaminated during shipping ______ the team discarded them and repeated the entire experiment with fresh cultures.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Steps by season
passages.text:
A study measured the average number of steps taken per day by adults in three age groups during summer and winter.
Age group | Summer | Winter
20–39 | 8,200 | 7,600
40–59 | 7,500 | 6,700
60 and older | 6,400 | 4,800
The researchers claim that the drop in daily steps from summer to winter was largest for adults aged 60 and older.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: The rehearsal
passages.text:
The following text is from a short story.
The orchestra had rehearsed the symphony's final movement eleven times that week. On the twelfth run, the conductor lowered her baton halfway through, said nothing for a long moment, and then told the musicians to go home early. Several of them looked at one another, unsure whether they had played very badly or very well.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A trial semester
passages.text: When the school board reviewed the proposal to keep the public library open until 9 p.m., its response was ______: members praised the plan's goals but voted to fund only a one-semester trial before committing to a permanent change.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Beaten thin
passages.text: Gold is unusually ______: a single gram of it can be hammered into a sheet nearly one square meter in area without tearing, a property that has made gold leaf a favorite of artists and bookbinders for centuries.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Worms that came later
passages.text: For much of the twentieth century, many gardeners and naturalists in the northern United States and Canada assumed that the earthworms in local forests had always lived there. Studies of species and their histories, however, indicate that most earthworms in these northern forests arrived from Europe and Asia in soil and plants carried by settlers, because the glaciers of the last ice age had largely wiped out native earthworms in the region. Ecologists now study how these newcomers alter the leaf litter and soil of forests that developed without them.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Narrow rings
passages.text: Researchers examining tree rings in a mountain valley found that pines on dry, south-facing slopes formed unusually narrow rings for an entire decade in the 1800s. Pines of the same species growing beside the valley's river, where groundwater is always available, formed rings of normal width during the same decade. These findings suggest that the narrow rings most likely reflect ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Three gardens
passages.text:
A city tracked three community gardens during one growing season.
Garden | Number of plots | Total harvest (kg)
A | 40 | 2,000
B | 25 | 1,500
C | 15 | 1,050
A city report claims that Garden C was the most productive per plot even though it had the fewest plots.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A farmer's find
passages.text: The silver coins, ______ in 1903 by a farmer plowing a field near the river, are now displayed at the county museum alongside the farmer's own account of the discovery.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Three generations
passages.text: Marisol Vega's 2015 novel The Orchards ______ the story of three generations of a family who run a fruit farm in central California, moving back and forth among their perspectives.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A fish without eyes
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Ozark cavefish is a small, pale fish with no functional eyes.
• It lives in caves and underground streams.
• Its range is limited to parts of Missouri, Arkansas, and Oklahoma.
• It is listed as threatened under the US Endangered Species Act.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Eleven prototypes
passages.text: Although her first designs failed every field test, the engineer remained ______, rebuilding and retesting the water filter eleven times over three years until it finally met the village council's standard.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Weighing two readings
passages.text: Reviewers praised the historian's account of the 1848 uprising as ______: it lays out the strengths of both rival interpretations of the event before cautiously favoring one of them.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Lights on the beach
passages.text: Newly hatched sea turtles find the ocean by heading toward the brightest part of the horizon, which on an undeveloped beach is usually the open sky above the water. Along developed coastlines, however, streetlights and lit windows can be brighter than the sea, and hatchlings may crawl inland, where many die. In response, a number of coastal towns now require residents to shield or turn off outdoor lights visible from the beach during nesting season.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Folding leaves
passages.text: Botanist Lena Ortiz hypothesizes that a desert shrub folds its leaves in the hottest part of the day mainly to reduce the amount of water the leaves lose.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A quieter motor
passages.text: After two years of development, the appliance maker announced that ______ new electric motor for washing machines runs about 40 percent more quietly than the model it replaces.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: An old crossing
passages.text: The Fennick River ferry carried passengers and freight for nearly a century before the county built a bridge at the same crossing in 1931, ______ remains in daily use and was widened in 1978.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A field without a plow
passages.text: For generations, farmers in the region prepared their fields each spring by plowing the soil deeply. ______ a growing number now plant directly into the stubble of the previous crop, a practice that leaves the soil undisturbed and helps it hold water.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Glass frogs
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Glass frogs live in the rainforests of Central and South America.
• Many have skin on their undersides so transparent that their hearts and other organs are visible.
• When glass frogs sleep, most of their red blood cells move into the liver.
• This makes the frogs about two to three times more transparent while they rest.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Listening plants
passages.text: Some plants appear to respond to the vibrations made by insects feeding on them. ______ in one experiment, thale cress plants that had been exposed to recorded vibrations of caterpillars chewing produced more of a defensive chemical when caterpillars later fed on them than plants that had not been exposed to such vibrations did.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Who has seen the wind?
passages.text: "Who Has Seen the Wind?" is an 1872 poem by Christina Rossetti. In the poem, the speaker suggests that the wind's presence can be known through its effects on the natural world.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Brief blooms
passages.text: Some desert wildflowers are strikingly ______: after a rare heavy rain they sprout, bloom, and drop their seeds within a few weeks, then disappear from the landscape until the next downpour, which may be years away.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A cautious announcement
passages.text: In interviews about her team's discovery, the astronomer's tone was notably ______: she called the result "interesting" rather than "groundbreaking" and repeatedly stressed how much remained unknown.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Safety in numbers
passages.text: Periodical cicadas in parts of North America spend 13 or 17 years underground as nymphs and then emerge by the millions within a few weeks. This timing is not a coincidence. Birds and other predators can eat only a small fraction of such an enormous swarm, so most of the cicadas survive long enough to mate, a strategy biologists call predator satiation.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A regular dip
passages.text: Astronomers observing a distant star found that its brightness dropped by the same small amount every 12.4 days, with each dip lasting about three hours. Random changes on a star's surface do not repeat on such a precise schedule. The astronomers therefore concluded that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Litter by type
passages.text:
Volunteers counted the litter collected during an annual beach cleanup. The town banned single-use plastic bags in 2022.
Litter type | 2021 | 2023
Plastic bottles | 420 | 210
Cigarette butts | 650 | 600
Plastic bags | 300 | 90
A local report claims that, from 2021 to 2023, plastic bags showed the largest percentage decrease of any litter type in the table.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: One hand or two? (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
A historian argues that a fourteenth-century manuscript of sermons was copied entirely by a single scribe, citing the remarkably consistent shape of the letters from the first page to the last.

Text 2
Scribes trained in the same workshop were taught to imitate a single house style so closely that their hands can be hard to tell apart. In this manuscript, analysis of the parchment shows that the last third was made from animal skins prepared differently from those used in the first two-thirds.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Mountain pastures
passages.text: Each spring, the ______ of the valley drive their goats up to the high pastures, where the animals graze until the first snow.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Above all
passages.text: The expedition's success depended on one thing more than any other ______ the weather in the narrow window when the pass would be free of ice.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Inefficient but indispensable
passages.text: The earliest steam engines were enormously inefficient, turning only a tiny fraction of the energy in their fuel into useful work. ______ they transformed mining in eighteenth-century Britain, because they could pump water out of deep mines far faster than teams of horses could.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Refill stations
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In 2023, Ridgeview High School installed four water-bottle refill stations.
• Sales of bottled water in Ridgeview's cafeteria fell by 40 percent that year.
• Each station cost about $1,500 to install.
• The district's two other high schools have no refill stations.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: One shared style
passages.text: The proposed link between the two ancient settlements remains ______: it rests entirely on a single shared pottery style, which could just as easily have spread between unrelated communities through trade.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Slow gains
passages.text: Rather than arriving in a sudden breakthrough, the improvement in phone battery life over the past decade has been ______, with each new generation lasting only slightly longer than the one before it.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A risky descent
passages.text: Three-toed sloths spend nearly all their lives in trees, yet about once a week they climb down to the ground to defecate, a trip that exposes them to predators. Researchers have found that moths living in sloth fur lay their eggs in the dung. The moths later return to the fur, where they appear to add nutrients that help algae grow there, and sloths sometimes eat that algae. Based on these findings, the researchers proposed that the risky descent ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Three wheat varieties
passages.text:
Researchers grew three varieties of wheat on 10 farms and recorded each variety's yield, in metric tons per hectare.
Variety | Average yield | Lowest yield | Highest yield
A | 4.1 | 3.8 | 4.4
B | 4.3 | 3.6 | 4.9
C | 4.6 | 2.9 | 6.0
The researchers claim that variety C produced the highest yields on average but was also the least consistent from farm to farm.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Composed on the spot? (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
A music critic describes jazz improvisation as composition in its purest form: a soloist invents an entirely new melody in the moment, with nothing prepared in advance.

Text 2
Studies of recorded jazz solos have found that experienced players frequently reuse short melodic phrases, often called licks, that they practiced beforehand. Skilled improvisers combine and vary these familiar phrases in new ways as they respond to the music around them.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A first program
passages.text: Ada Lovelace, a mathematician by ______ wrote in 1843 a set of notes on a proposed calculating machine that included what many historians consider the first published computer program.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Sold out
passages.text: By noon the bakery had sold every loaf of bread ______ by evening, even the last tray of pastries was gone.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Trees and fire
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The cones of lodgepole pines are often sealed with resin that melts in the heat of a fire, releasing seeds onto the burned ground.
• Jack pines also have cones that open mainly after exposure to fire.
• Some eucalyptus trees sprout new shoots from buds under their bark after a fire.
• All three kinds of trees grow in places where wildfires occur regularly.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Prices without minutes
passages.text: No rule in the guild's charter forbade members from undercutting one another's prices, yet historians believe members observed a ______ understanding on the matter: the records of guild meetings never mention prices at all, but members' prices stayed within a few pennies of one another for decades.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A small jaw
passages.text: The fossil's modest size ______ its significance: the jaw, barely two centimeters long, preserves a pattern of tooth replacement that researchers had predicted for fish of its age but had never before observed.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: A relay across generations
passages.text: Each fall, monarch butterflies from eastern North America fly thousands of kilometers to forests in central Mexico, where they spend the winter. In spring they head north, but no individual completes the return. The butterflies breed along the way, and it is their children and grandchildren that continue the journey and reach the northern United States and Canada. The monarchs that fly south again in the fall may therefore be the great-grandchildren of those that left Mexico in spring.
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Urban coyotes
passages.text: Food from people, such as garbage and pet food, is plentiful in cities and takes little effort for coyotes to obtain, so one might expect urban coyotes that eat it to be healthier than coyotes that hunt. A 2015 study in Edmonton, Canada, found the reverse: coyotes whose diets included more human food were in poorer body condition and more likely to have mange. One possible explanation is that human food, though plentiful, is low in the protein that coyotes need, which would mean that ______
passages.author: ai:claude

passages.title: Window treatments
passages.text:
Researchers recorded the average number of bird collisions per month at office buildings before and after one of three window treatments was installed.
Treatment | Before | After
Dot-pattern film | 20 | 6
UV-reflective glass | 40 | 22
Exterior netting | 10 | 4
The researchers concluded that, relative to each building group's starting level, the dot-pattern film was the most effective of the three treatments.

passages.title: Following a point (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
In experiments where a person points to one of two cups hiding food, pet dogs choose the correct cup far more often than chimpanzees do. Some researchers have concluded that domestication gave dogs an inborn sensitivity to human gestures that their wild relatives lack.
Text 2
Other researchers have found that wolves raised by people from birth can follow pointing about as well as pet dogs, while shelter dogs with little human contact often struggle with the task. These researchers argue that a dog's experience with people shapes this skill more than has been recognized.

passages.title: Draupner wave
passages.text: For decades, sailors' reports of "rogue waves" (single waves more than twice as tall as the surrounding seas) were often dismissed as exaggerations, since standard models predicted that such waves should be extremely rare. Then, on January 1, 1995, a laser sensor on the Draupner oil platform in the North Sea recorded a wave about 26 meters high amid seas of roughly 12 meters. Researchers have since revised their models, and satellite surveys suggest rogue waves are more common than once believed.

passages.title: Monsters at sea (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
The sea serpents and whales that decorate many medieval and Renaissance maps have often been read as warnings. On this view, mapmakers drew monsters in waters they considered dangerous or poorly known, telling sailors, in effect, to beware.
Text 2
A historian of cartography who traced many of these creatures to the natural-history books of the period argues that mapmakers usually believed such animals really lived where they drew them. The creatures, he suggests, were often a way of recording what was thought to be known about the oceans, and of showing off the mapmaker's skill, more than a way of marking danger.

Although the wall is extremely long, it is only a few meters wide and is built from materials close in color to the land around it. Highways and airport runways, which are wider and contrast more with their surroundings, are far easier to spot.

passages.title: Rising at the end (two texts)
passages.text:
Text 1
In many varieties of English, some speakers end statements with a rise in pitch, as if asking a question. Critics of this habit, often called uptalk, argue that it signals uncertainty and makes speakers sound less confident than they are.
Text 2
Linguists who have analyzed recorded conversations report that speakers often use this rising pitch on statements they are clearly sure of, such as when giving directions or listing facts. In those settings, the rise seems to work as a check, inviting the listener to signal that they are following.

passages.title: A raven's plan
passages.text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• In a 2017 study, researchers taught ravens to use a stone tool to open a box containing food.
• Later, with the box out of sight, each raven was offered the tool among several useless objects.
• Most ravens picked the tool and kept it.
• The researchers tested delays of 15 minutes and of 17 hours before returning the box.
• When the box was returned, as much as 17 hours later, the ravens used the tool to open it.
• Planning for a future need is rare among animals.
